topic: Glaw Lake becomes India's 101st Ramsar Site

subtopics.title: Wetlands: Meaning and Types
subtopics.summary: A wetland is an area of land covered by water, whether salt, fresh or in between, either seasonally or permanently. Wetlands take many forms, from lakes and rivers to mangroves and coral reefs. The booklet classifies them into three segments: inland, coastal and human-made wetlands.
facts: Wetland: land covered by water that is salt, fresh or in between
The water cover may be seasonal or permanent
Includes lakes, rivers, underground aquifers and swamps
Includes wet grasslands, peatlands, deltas and tidal flats
Includes mangroves, coral reefs and other coastal areas
Other forms: marshes, bogs, mudflats, ponds, billabongs, lagoons, floodplains

subtopics.title: Ramsar Convention and Montreux Record
subtopics.summary: The Ramsar Convention, formally the Convention on Wetlands of International Importance, is an intergovernmental treaty adopted in 1971 in Ramsar, Iran, and in force from 1975. It has 172 member states, and India became a signatory on 1 February 1982. The Montreux Record, launched in 1990, lists Ramsar sites where ecological character has changed or is likely to change.
facts: Official name: Convention on Wetlands of International Importance
Adopted in 1971 in Ramsar, Iran; came into force in 1975
India became a signatory on 1 February 1982
2026 theme: Wetlands and Traditional Knowledge: Celebrating Cultural Heritage
Conference of Parties (COP) meets every 3 years
Montreux Record: launched 1990; lists sites with ecological change from technological developments, pollution or human interference
Indian sites in Montreux Record: Keoladeo National Park (Rajasthan) and Loktak Lake (Manipur)
Largest Ramsar site in the world: Pantanal, South America
